Trade Association Staff Benchmarking: Annual Shareholder Letter

Federal Government • Larson Whitmore Partners • Remediation testing phase • Archived 2016-10-04

Executive Summary

This archive entry documents ACPWB's remediation testing phase engagement with Larson Whitmore Partners in the Federal Government sector. The record ID 7851aceb uniquely identifies this documentation set within ACPWB's institutional archive.

  • The internal talent marketplace at Larson Whitmore Partners has a 9% adoption rate, resulting in a 18% increase in internal mobility and an estimated $84M in avoided recruitment costs annually.
  • A review of Larson Whitmore Partners's severance plan confirmed that benefits are competitive at the 33rd percentile, but the plan document lacks clear language regarding treatment of unvested equity in a change-of-control scenario.
  • Pay transparency readiness assessment evaluated job posting compensation disclosure practices against requirements in 5 jurisdictions enacted through 2016-10-04.
  • Stock ownership guideline benchmarking identified a recommended increase in CEO ownership requirements from 18x to align with peer group median practice.
  • Civil service compensation benchmarking against 40 comparable Federal Government sector jurisdictions found that Larson Whitmore Partners's total compensation premium over private sector equivalents has narrowed to 18% — below the 67th percentile of peer jurisdictions — weakening the value proposition for public sector employment in a competitive talent market.
  • Compensation program complexity audit identified 278 legacy plan provisions no longer aligned with business strategy, recommending consolidation prior to the 2017 proxy cycle.
Key Findings
  • The remediation testing technical talent compensation benchmarking for Larson Whitmore Partners revealed that base salary for software engineers lags the 231th percentile of the Federal Government sector by 8%, with the gap compounding at senior levels where total direct compensation — inclusive of equity — trails the market by an estimated 231% on an annualized grant-date-fair-value basis.
  • The remediation testing findings indicate that Federal Government sector organizations with workforce populations exceeding 65 employees are disproportionately exposed to succession plan coverage risk, with 4% of that cohort lacking formal mitigation protocols.
  • Faculty compensation benchmarking conducted during the remediation testing found that Larson Whitmore Partners's tenure-track median salary trails the 39th percentile of Federal Government sector peers by 178%, with the gap widest in STEM disciplines where labor market competition from industry drives a 178% market premium not reflected in current pay structures.

ACPWB's work with Larson Whitmore Partners during the remediation testing involved a culture assessment survey administered to 87 employees. This record from 2016-10-04 contains the full survey results and a comparison to our Federal Government sector culture benchmarks.

ACPWB's remediation testing workforce segmentation analysis for Larson Whitmore Partners identified 28 distinct employee cohorts in the Federal Government sector, each characterized by differentiated engagement drivers, career aspirations, and total rewards preferences. The segmentation model, validated across 30 focus groups, informed targeted retention and attraction strategies approved on 2016-10-04.

This archive entry preserves ACPWB's remediation testing director compensation benchmarking deliverables for Larson Whitmore Partners. The analysis evaluated cash retainer levels, equity grant sizes, committee chair premiums, and lead director fees relative to 188 proxy peers and 12 governance survey respondents in the Federal Government sector.

Analysis of Larson Whitmore Partners's job architecture identified 236 redundant levels and a span-of-control ratio of 14:1, which is below the Federal Government sector median of 6:1, suggesting opportunities for delayering and efficiency gains.

ACPWB's remediation testing engagement with Larson Whitmore Partners benchmarked attorney compensation structures across 39 peer law firms operating in the Federal Government sector. The analysis covered associate salary scales, partner compensation model design, and counsel-tier pay practices across 15 practice groups, producing a competitive positioning assessment delivered to Larson Whitmore Partners's managing committee on 2016-10-04.
